duplicate-member/json.reason: Go JSON decoding keeps the last duplicate member; SenWeave rejects duplicates.

unknown-version/cbor.reason: Go carries bver=99 without an unsupported-feature check; SenWeave currently supports version 10.

uppercase-exponent/json.reason: Go accepts uppercase E; SenML JSON requires lowercase e (RFC 8428 section 5).

integer-53/json.reason: Go uses binary64 and loses exact integer representation. Binary64 equivalence is checked separately; exact integer preservation is an additional SenWeave capability.

integer-53/cbor.reason: Go uses binary64 and loses exact integer representation. Binary64 equivalence is checked separately; exact integer preservation is an additional SenWeave capability.

uint64-max/json.reason: Go uses binary64 and loses exact integer representation. Binary64 equivalence is checked separately; exact integer preservation is an additional SenWeave capability.

uint64-max/cbor.reason: Go uses binary64 and loses exact integer representation. Binary64 equivalence is checked separately; exact integer preservation is an additional SenWeave capability.

negative-cbor-min/json.reason: The JSON spelling changes after binary64 formatting. The CBOR float still represents -2^64 exactly; this is a representation distinction, not evidence of a different binary64 measurement.

negative-cbor-min/cbor.reason: The pinned CBOR decoder rejects the valid major-type-1 value -2^64 when converting through int64.

base-value-on-sum/json.reason: Normalize does not apply bv when a sum-only measurement has no regular v (RFC 8428 section 4.5.4).

base-value-on-sum/cbor.reason: Normalize does not apply bv when a sum-only measurement has no regular v (RFC 8428 section 4.5.4).

integral-version-decimal/json.reason: JSON 10.0 has an integral value; Go uint decoding accepts only integer lexical form.

decimal-tag-four/cbor.reason: The pinned Go decoder cannot convert the standard Tag 4 decimal fraction to its float64 value.

arithmetic-overflow/json.reason: SenWeave rejects non-finite addition during resolve. Go Normalize succeeds with +Inf; its JSON encoder rejects the result later.
